newsitem.title: CANADA: CS Resources rises on PanCanadian offer.
newsitem.headline: CS Resources rises on PanCanadian offer.

text.p: Shares of CS Resources Ltd jumped C$1 to reach C$15.95 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday after PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said it would offer C$16 a share cash for all of the Calgary-based petroleum heavy oil producer.

PanCanadian said its offer included C$56 million of debt and had a total purchase price of C$521 million. PanCanadian, which 87-percent-owned by Montreal-based Canadian Pacific Ltd, said its offer represented a 17 percent premium to the cash and share offer for CS Resources made by Gulf Canada Resources Ltd.

More than 2 million shares of CS Resources had traded within 30 minutes of the TSE opening on Wednesday. Shares of Gulf Canada were up C$0.30 to reach C$12 on a volume of more than 345,000 shares. PanCanadian shares were up C$0.20 to reach C$30.40 on very thin volume.
In a statement, Dennis Sharp, chairman and chief executive of CS Resources, said he thought the PanCanadian offer was a "fair price."

PanCanadian said it planned to mail its offer to CS Resources shareholders on or about June 20 and the bid will expire 24 days later. The offer is conditional on 66-2/3 percent of CS Resources outstanding shares being tendered.
